findings.title: A pre-resume worker meter cut still permits target resume
findings.counterexample: The target is established suspended. Worker0 signals started, then its first WorkerRead ticket refuses, setting refused/tail and freezing the prefix under the meter lock. start_workers can subsequently spend WorkerStart in tail: charge initializes ok=true and skips its prefix branch, so the second worker is created and start_workers returns true. supervisor_main unconditionally marks TargetMayHaveRun and attempts ResumeThread on ready, with no body admission/cut test. The coordinator then immediately notices tail and enters cleanup. Thus a fresh target-resume action is attempted after the cut; it was not a native call admitted before that cut.
findings.obligation: Protocol v1 sections8/10: first refusal enters the mandatory cleanup/publication tail; no new body admission after the linearized cut. The tail is not permission to begin target execution or create new body activity after refusal.
findings.required_correction: Give target resume and worker startup an explicit body-admission decision that distinguishes a pre-cut admitted operation from prepaid cleanup. A cut observed before resume must keep the established target suspended and settle it via the existing pre-execution failure route. Preserve publication/accounting of already acquired/completed results and the separate actual TargetMayHaveRun ordering. Review analogous setup/body seams, without new allowances, limits, input-domain restrictions or target execution.
